name: Herod Antipas
bio: Herod the tetrarch (Herod Antipas), son of Herod the Great, imprisoned John the Baptist at the urging of his wife Herodias after John condemned their marriage, though he feared the crowds who honored John as a prophet and hesitated to kill him. At a birthday banquet, Herodias's daughter danced for him, and he rashly swore to grant her any request; prompted by her mother, she asked for John's head, and Herod reluctantly had him beheaded. When he later heard of Jesus's growing fame, he feared John had risen from the dead (Matthew 14:1-12). When Pilate learned that Jesus was a Galilean, he sent him to Herod, who was in Jerusalem at the time; Herod, long curious to see Jesus perform a miracle, questioned him at length, but Jesus gave no answer. Herod and his soldiers mocked Jesus, dressed him in a gorgeous robe, and sent him back to Pilate; the episode reconciled Pilate and Herod, who had previously been at odds (Luke 23:6-12).
